items.title: Solomon Pappaiah, Tamil scholar and celebrated Pattimandram moderator, dies at 90
items.summary: Renowned Tamil scholar and veteran Pattimandram moderator Solomon Pappaiah died at a private hospital in Madurai on Friday, September 11, following age-related health complications. He was 90. Pappaiah had been undergoing treatment for several days after his health deteriorated, with his family confirming his death at the hospital. For several generations of Tamil television viewers, Pappaiah was a familiar face associated with Pattimandram, the traditional Tamil debate format in which speakers argue opposing sides of a literary, social or cultural topic. As a moderator, he helped take the format beyond academic and literary circles and into homes across Tamil Nadu and among Tamil-speaking audiences elsewhere. Pappaiah was a former Tamil professor at The American College in Madurai and became one of Tamil Nadu’s best-known debate moderators, taking literary and social discussions to a wider television audience. His ability to combine humour with serious literary and social commentary made him particularly popular with television audiences. items.title: ADR should not become a privilege for those who can afford it: Justice Sandeep Mehta
items.summary: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) should not become a privilege available only to parties who can afford sophisticated dispute resolution mechanisms, Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta said on Thursday. Justice Mehta said the success of ADR could not be measured merely by speed, efficiency or the number of institutions established. “ ADR should not become a privilege, available only to those who can afford the cost of sophisticated dispute resolution, ” he said. The judge was speaking at the Delhi chapter of India ADR Week 2026 , organised by the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). Justice Mehta said cost and accessibility were equally important. If dispute resolution became excessively expensive, it could itself become a barrier of the kind ADR was intended to remove. He also referred to the move away from arbitration in some government contracts. The dispute resolution ecosystem, he said, must remain sophisticated without becoming unnecessarily expensive. Justice Mehta stressed that ADR was not synonymous with arbitration. Arbitration, mediation, conciliation, negotiation and Lok Adalats were different mechanisms suited to different disputes. items.title: Navigating Commercial Disputes with Payal Chawla: Episode 9 - Senior Advocate Meenakshi Arora
items.summary: Navigating Commercial Disputes is a video podcast hosted by disputes lawyer Payal Chawla in collaboration with Bar & Bench. Drawing on her experience in arbitration and corporate law, Chawla aims to unpack the law and the intricacies surrounding commercial disputes, with incisive insights. Tailored for lawyers, law students, and legal enthusiasts alike, each episode offers listeners a fresh perspective on the subject. In this ninth episode, Payal Chawla speaks to Senior Advocate Meenakshi Arora on whether certain aspects of matrimonial disputes in India, particularly financial, property, maintenance and visitation issues, could be resolved through arbitration, while leaving rights and issues in rem firmly within the domain of the courts. Drawing on international models, including family arbitration in England and Wales, the conversation examines whether a carefully designed arbitral framework could offer Indian families a faster, more specialised and efficacious route to dispute resolution.
